An app to check Italian train times in real time, using the same data as ViaggiaTreno (Trenitalia). No account, no ads: open it, search, check your train.
Type the station name and pick it from the suggestions. You can see Departures or Arrivals, and choose a time other than \"now\" by tapping the clock button.

If you also add a destination (or origin), the app only shows the trains that actually get there — including those that need a change along the way, telling you where to get off and which train to take next.
Type the number to see all the stops of that train, with scheduled and actual times, delay and where it is right now. It also works for a train that left hours ago.

Italo trains are not tracked by ViaggiaTreno: if the number isn\'t found there, the app automatically tries Italo\'s data source. It is an unofficial and less complete source (no station boards, train number search only), so the data shown for Italo may be less detailed or occasionally unavailable.
The latest origin→destination pairs and train numbers you searched are saved as shortcuts, so you don\'t have to type everything again when you\'re in a hurry.
The list refreshes by itself every minute. There\'s also a manual refresh button (🔄) if you want to be sure you have the very latest data right away.
⏳ A limitation to know about: searching the past
If you search for a train by NUMBER, the app can show it even hours after it left: that data stays available for the whole day.

If you search by STATION, things are different: that list is a sort of \"live departure board\", tied to the actual current time — it isn\'t an archive you can browse. If you ask for a time more than a couple of hours ago, the board comes back empty, because that data simply doesn\'t exist anywhere anymore (it\'s not the app\'s fault: Trenitalia itself doesn\'t provide it).

There\'s one exception: if the app has already shown those trains during this session (for example with \"now\"), it keeps them in memory and lets you see them again even after they\'ve left. But if you open the app and immediately ask for a past time without the app ever having seen those trains live, you\'re better off searching by train number instead of by station.
The ☀️/🌙 button at the top switches the theme: dark for the evening, light for comfortable use in sunlight. Your choice is saved.
The \"Aa\" button at the top lets you choose between Normal, Large and Extra large, for anyone who has trouble reading small text. This choice is saved too.

TreniRT is an independent, hobby project, not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Trenitalia, RFI, Gruppo FS or Italo (NTV). It uses the same public data from the ViaggiaTreno infrastructure available on the official website and app, but it is not an official product and does not guarantee its accuracy.
